findings.problem: RouteWorkflow uses no state machine at all — status is a String and lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent) are independent flags, so callers can construct illegal state combinations like status="draft" with is_sent=true simultaneously.
findings.failure_mode: State invariants are unenforceable at the type level; the struct can represent impossible combinations (validated but not sent, sent but invalid status string, etc.), violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Replace with a Rust enum typestate (e.g., enum RouteState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }) and remove is_validated, is_sent, and status fields entirely.

findings.problem: status field is pub String — any caller can set it to any value ("foo", "SENT", "", null bytes), and mark_sent mutates it to "sent".ts at line 10 with no state precondition check.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants encoded as free-form strings are unenforceable; invalid status values propagate silently through the system and break downstream assumptions.
findings.fix: Replace with a closed enum (e.g., pub enum RouteStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }) and make status a single field of that enum type.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be set in any combination, decoupled from status. The type system cannot enforce that validation precedes sending.
findings.failure_mode: A RouteWorkflow can be constructed with is_validated=false and is_sent=true, or is_validated=true and is_sent=false, and mark_sent does not check is_validated before setting is_sent.
findings.fix: Encode lifecycle as typestate transitions: use an enum where Sent variant owns sent_at_epoch_ms, Validated owns nothing extra, and Draft is initial. Transitions go through named methods on each variant.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a detached optional field, not tied to any state. It can be Some(value) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true, and there is no invariant linking them.
findings.failure_mode: Optional lifecycle data lives outside the variant that owns it; callers can leave sent_at_epoch_ms as None when is_sent=true, or set a timestamp without marking sent, creating inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of an enum: Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. Only the Sent variant holds the timestamp — it is always Some by construction.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain rules, format, length constraint, or uniqueness guarantee. It is a public field directly accessible by any caller.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicate IDs, or unvalidated identifiers can enter the domain. No smart constructor or validation exists at the boundary.
findings.fix: Create a newtype: pub struct RouteId(String) or better pub struct RouteId(u64) with a smart constructor that validates format/length and returns a typed error on invalid input.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts raw RouteWorkflow with no preconditions — it does not validate that is_validated is true before marking sent, does not check current status, and callers can construct any invalid RouteWorkflow directly via pub fields. Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller with a RouteWorkflow can mark it as sent regardless of validation state, bypassing the workflow invariant that a route must be validated before sending. No boundary parsing or factory method exists.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a method on a typestate enum (e.g., RouteState::Validated.into_sent()) that is only callable on the Validated variant, and provide fallible smart constructors at the boundary to create valid RouteWorkflow instances.
